_readme: Auralis in-app copy. Edit the live fields below, save, and the app picks them up on next launch (cached — allow a minute). _changelog records what each field said BEFORE and what it ships as NOW, so you can restore any of it exactly. Human-readable view: https://aytekinc.github.io/auralis-legal/config.html — WARNING: whatever you put here is a public claim. Guideline 2.3.1 requires in-app claims to be accurate (a rating or user count that does not exist is grounds for removal, not just rejection); 1.1.1 forbids mean-spirited content. An empty string hides that element.

_changelog.why: The app labelled the user's own face. 'Low Tier Normie' on the results screen is the first thing a reviewer sees.
_changelog.note: 5 entries, lowest to highest. Thresholds stay in code: 52 / 66 / 78 / 88.

_changelog.why: The app is not published yet, so it has no App Store rating. Showing one is grounds for removal.
_changelog.note: Turn on once your product page actually shows a rating. If the number is not from the App Store, say so in ratingCaption (e.g. 'Rated by our early testers').

_changelog.why: Invented totals. Empty hides the elements and the screens fall back to verifiable facts (20 measurements, 7 categories, 39 lessons).
_changelog.note: A green pill also read '225 scans in the last 24 hours'; it now reads 'Nothing leaves your device'.

_changelog.why: The counter starts at 187 and increments on a 9-second timer — it is not real data.
_changelog.note: When false the plan-page footer shows 'Everything is measured and stored on your device'.

_changelog.why: The quotes are written, not collected. The badge makes that visible instead of implying real reviews.
_changelog.note: Adds a visible 'Illustrative example' badge. Set false only for quotes from real, consenting users. The reviews step header also changed from 'Trusted by Thousands' + 'Over 75,000+ members'.

_changelog.why: Quotes 1 and 4 promised specific measured outcomes from people who do not exist.

_changelog.why: The engine measures 2D facial landmarks; depth-dependent metrics are flagged 'estimated'. Calling it a 3D scan overstates it.
_changelog.note: Related in-app strings changed with it: 'A precision 3D map of your features', 'A Live 3D Model of You', 'Your 3D face scan', 'Unlimited 3D Face Scans', 'Assembling your 3D profile…'.

_changelog.why: The onboarding paywall has no close button. Hard gates are allowed, but if the store cannot sell (products not approved, sandbox hiccup, no network) the user - and an App Review tester - is trapped on a screen that cannot succeed. That is the most common paywall rejection. The app now opens the gate automatically in that case; this flag lets you soften it everywhere without a build if review pushes back.
_changelog.note: TRUE  = hard paywall: no close button, no skip, the user must subscribe to enter the app. FALSE = normal paywall: close button and the escape action are always visible. The ONE exception to TRUE: if StoreKit has no purchasable product (products not approved yet, sandbox failure, no network) the close appears anyway, because otherwise the only button on the screen always fails and both your user and an App Review tester are trapped — that is the Guideline 2.1 rejection. Whenever the store can actually sell, TRUE means no way out. escapeLabel sets the wording of that action.
